priority.description: Priority order when recommending Dialtone solutions

details.component: Always prefer specific Vue components when one fits the use case (e.g., DtButton over composing a button manually)
details.primitive: When no specific component fits, reach for the primitive triad — DtBox (surface, padding, border, shadow, sizing, simple token-backed positioning), DtStack (layout: direction, gap, alignment), DtText (typography) — before composing with utility classes
details.utility-class: Use utility classes for styling concerns the primitives intentionally don't cover (display, grid, flex-child, etc.), for positioning outside DtBox's prop surface (responsive, calc, reset, arbitrary coordinates, non-DtBox elements, etc.), or for surgical adjustments (e.g., d-pie-25 for padding-inline-end)
details.token: Write custom CSS only when components, primitives, and utilities don't fit; when you do, use design tokens instead of hard-coded values.

details.semantic: Prefer semantic color tokens (e.g., --dt-color-foreground-tertiary, --dt-color-surface-positive) over base colors. Components and primitives like DtBox already use semantic tokens internally — these guidelines apply when you're writing raw CSS.
details.base: Direct use of base color tokens (e.g., --dt-color-purple-600) is deprecated: they don't adapt to brand or contrast modes. Prefer semantic tokens; if none fit the use case, consult a Product Designer before using base colors.

details.dt-text: In Vue templates, prefer the DtText component for individual authored text elements. Use `variant` prop for a complete typography composition (e.g., <dt-text variant="body-sm">), with tone for semantic color. Add size only when a raw font-size token override is needed; kind+size remains supported for legacy compatibility. Part of the primitive triad alongside DtBox and DtStack.
details.typography-class: Use typography utility classes (e.g., d-text-body--md) or complete typography tokens (e.g., --dt-text-body-md) for non-Vue HTML or as a class escape hatch when DtText doesn't fit
details.text-style-token: Use individual text style tokens (e.g., --dt-font-size-200, --dt-font-line-height-100) only for fine-tuned control in custom CSS when a complete typography composition doesn't fit.

search.description: How to search Dialtone documentation effectively
tips: Search by CSS property names: prefer logical names ('padding-block-start', 'margin-inline-end'). Physical direction queries also recover logical padding, margin and inset matches assuming horizontal-tb and left-to-right writing; verify the writing mode

Search by class name patterns (e.g., 'pbs-200', 'mie-100', 'd-mbs-auto'). Logical abbrevs: pbs/pbe (block-start/end), pis/pie (inline-start/end). Legacy 'pt'/'pr' aliases still emit but apply logical properties under the hood
Search by component API — the search indexes prop names, slot names, and event names (e.g., 'startIcon' for a prop, 'header' for a slot, 'update:open' for an event)
Use specific technical terms rather than natural language
